correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=7, the binary coordinate dot product equals the number of matching permutation positions modulo 2. The central character eigenvalue is n!/d times the Schur specialization with p1=z and pj=1 for j>=2. The elementary generating series (1+u)exp((z-1)u), the explicitly expanded dual Jacobi--Trudi determinant for lambda conjugate (n-4,3,1), and the hook-length formula prove Theta=(z-1)^{n-3}(z+1)(z^2+(n-4)z+n-1). The irreducible regular multiplicity d^2 yields the rigorous lower nullity bound. For n=7 a complete fifteen-partition exact census gives exactly one zero sector of degree 21, so nullity 441. The extracted standalone checker independently matches all polynomial coefficients for n=7..20, exhaustive sectors at n=4,5,7, and direct modular ranks n=2..5. Finite checks corroborate, not replace, the general proof.

originality.rationale: The same natural Fourier operator, fixed-point parity weights, stable Specht shape and explicit factor were compared against the closest published character and fixed-point literature. Derangement-graph eigenvalues concern the zero-fixed-point indicator; fixed-point polynomials without character weights are the trivial sector. General character calculus supplies the method but does not explicitly state the new cancellation and quantified Fourier nullspace. Related published symmetric-group Fourier-block results concern distinct kernels, not a statement covering this matrix. Bounded originality only; historical priority cannot be certified.

value.rationale: The fixed-position permutation matrices form a canonical structured subset of a binary matrix character group. Whether self-Fourier samples reconstruct arbitrary data supported on this set is a natural rank/stability question. The theorem gives a nontrivial, exact polynomially growing isotypic obstruction in every dimension n>=7, a sharp first stable boundary at n=7, and an exact phase-root explanation distinct from general dimension counting. It does not claim full spectra in every dimension or unrelated reconstruction consequences.
